title: Rav Ulla bar Abba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman calls him a very pious man. Sanhedrin 88b relates that they sent from there: “Who merits the world to come? One who is humble and lowly, enters modestly and leaves modestly, studies Torah constantly, and takes no credit for himself.” The sages directed their attention to Rav Ulla bar Abba.

In Hyman’s account of Ketubot 74a, Rav Ulla bar Abba speaks in Ulla’s name, and Ulla speaks in the name of R-H [אר״ה]. If so, Hyman places him approximately in the fourth generation of the Babylonian Amoraim.

notes.text: Ketubot 74a explicitly transmits Ulla’s saying from Rabbi Elazar. The supplied entry has אר״ה instead; that abbreviation is retained without inventing a Huna identification.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier Ketubot consultation names Elazar after Ulla; supplied אר״ה remains explicit without a new Huna identification or asserted aleph/he error history. ב״א expands locally to bar Abba from the heading. Hyman’s approximate fourth-generation placement remains conditional on the reporting chain. The commendation’s modest entry/exit, constant Torah study and refusal to take credit are preserved; it is not independently established chronology.

Hyman’s notice crosses pp. 974–975. The continuation actually prints אר״ה. The consulted Ketubot 74a instead gives Rav Ulla bar Abba reporting Ulla in the name of R’ Elazar. Sanhedrin 88b supplies the commendation of Rav Ulla bar Abba’s humility, regular study and refusal to take credit. Hyman’s approximate generation follows from how he reads the reporting chain.
